key_insight: LLMs can recognize updated medical guidance without fully incorporating it into their recommendations.
clinical_relevance: Awareness of guideline revisions alone may not ensure recommendations reflect current guidance, particularly when recommendation strength or patient eligibility changes.
method: Introduced ChronoEvo: 1,709 recommendation-level revisions across 12 types of medical knowledge change.
Evaluated recognition versus incorporation across 14 models, with two-clinician adjudication of 300 responses.
Tested an intervention that emphasized guideline revisions.
evidence_signal: The primary model recognized revisions in 90.8% of responses but fully incorporated them in 58.5%, a 32.3-percentage-point gap; clinician validation found a 40.3-point gap.
watch_item: Emphasizing revisions reduced outdated content and improved clinical correctness but did not significantly improve full incorporation, leaving reliability concerns even when updated evidence is available.
paper_title: Large language models show systematic failures in incorporating evolving medical knowledge
